record.paper_title: Constructing groups of 'small' order: Recent results and open problems
record.context_brief: Independent verification of computed group data
record.original_question: Can the remaining small-order group enumerations that lack an independent verification be cross-checked by a second method? The unresolved reliability target consists of six non-solvable cases that were not cross-checked and, on the solvable side, 183 orders below 20000 for which the solvable groups were enumerated by only one method, while another 39 orders still remained open for enumeration.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each positive integer $n$, let $g(n)$ denote the number of isomorphism classes of finite groups of order $n$. Various computational methods exist for enumerating and constructing representatives of these isomorphism classes (for example, the Frattini extension method for solvable groups, cyclic-extension methods, coclass-based methods, and methods for non-solvable groups built on top of classifications of simple and almost-simple groups). A computed enumeration $g(n)$ together with an explicit list of representatives is said to be "independently verified" if it has been obtained by at least two essentially different construction methods that agree.

Consider the following situation for orders $n \le 20000$:

(a) On the non-solvable side, there are exactly six orders $n \le 20000$ for which the groups of order $n$ have been constructed and counted by only one method, and no independent cross-check exists.

(b) On the solvable side, there are exactly $183$ orders $n \le 20000$ for which the solvable groups of order $n$ have been enumerated by only one method, with no second independent verification.

(c) In addition, there remain $39$ orders $n \le 20000$ for which a complete enumeration of all groups of order $n$ has not yet been carried out at all.

Problem: Provide a second, independent construction method that successfully cross-checks the existing enumerations in cases (a) and (b), thereby producing matching counts and isomorphism-class lists by two essentially different methods; and complete the enumeration of all groups of order $n$ for each of the $39$ orders $n \le 20000$ in case (c).
artifact.status_search_result: Search results indicate that the enumeration of groups of small order remains an active area, with the Small Groups Library covering most orders up to 20000 but with a small number of exceptional orders (notably orders divisible by 2^8·p^2 for small primes p) still resistant to complete construction. Subsequent work (e.g., the perfect groups of order up to two million, and counting supersolvable/solvable group orders, 2024) has reduced but not eliminated the list of unverified and unconstructed orders below 20000. No source found confirms full resolution of all six non-solvable cases, the 183 unverified solvable orders, and the 39 open orders.

status_evidence.title: Constructing Groups of 'Small' Order: Recent Results and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists open problems and orders below 20000 lacking independent verification or enumeration.
status_evidence.claim: Identifies six non-solvable orders without cross-check, 183 solvable orders verified by only one method, and 39 orders open for enumeration.

status_evidence.title: SmallGrp - The GAP Small Groups Library 1.5.4 (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Documents the current state of the Small Groups Library, with orders up to 2000 fully covered and partial information for higher orders.
status_evidence.claim: As of the most recent SmallGrp release (July 2024), some orders below 20000 remain not fully classified.

status_evidence.title: Counting supersolvable and solvable group orders (2024)
status_evidence.snippet: Recent counting results for solvable group orders.
status_evidence.claim: Progress has been made on solvable enumeration but the verification gap persists.
